children: Shares of InterGlobe Aviation were trading 4.52 per cent higher at ₹5,675.50 on the NSE by 12.54 pm on Wednesday, with the intraday high touching ₹5,713. The stock opened at ₹5,520.40 against a previous close of ₹5,430 and has already breached the ₹5,550 target price set by Anand Rathi Securities. Traded volume stood at 14.90 lakh shares, with a traded value of ₹844.24 crore by early afternoon.

Anand Rathi maintained a BUY on InterGlobe Aviation in a note dated October 31, valuing the stock at 9.5x FY28e EBITDA. The brokerage cited IndiGo’s dominant market position, approximately ₹399bn in free cash as of Q2FY27, and weak competition — with rivals Air India, Akasa, and SpiceJet each facing operational or financial stress — as the basis for their positive stance. The company followed up with an analyst and institutional investor meet on November 4, the last leg of post-results engagement before the Diwali Balipratipada holiday closed markets on November 10.

Wednesday’s immediate trigger appears to be a drop in crude oil. Brent futures for January fell 1.44 per cent to $90.75 a barrel in early trade after US officials played down the possibility of fresh military action involving Iran, easing supply disruption fears. Fuel is one of IndiGo’s largest cost heads, so cheaper crude directly improves the near-term margin outlook.

The broader market added to the tailwind. Sensex opened over 1,142 points higher at 82,248.68 and Nifty started at 25,337.80, both resuming after the holiday. IndiGo was among the top Nifty 50 gainers.

The move builds on Q2FY27 results released on October 31, which showed revenue rising approximately 25.9 per cent year-on-year to ₹233.6bn, beating estimates by about 3.1 per cent. Passenger yields jumped 34.3 per cent to ₹6.30 per km. However, EBITDA fell roughly 6.7 per cent to ₹32.4bn as fuel costs surged about 67.2 per cent year-on-year due to the West Asia conflict.
The stock has gained 17.49 per cent over the past month and 10.46 per cent over the past week. Its 52-week high stands at ₹5,970.

title: IndiGo surges past analyst target as crude slide and Q2 beat draw buyers
